rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a supplementary/lookup page, so the reading-list/lookup-surface carve-out waives the per-slide <=1-bold budget -- but the handle cap (<=5 words, a SUB-SPAN, never a whole lead sentence) still binds and is violated on every bullet in both flagged chunks, unchanged by the pinned diff (which touched only chunk 1). Chunk 5 '## Design principles' (115-126): all 7 bullets bold a complete lead clause ending in a period, e.g. line 119 '**A skill never duplicates another's logic.** `/tdd` references `/testing`...' (bold span = 7 words, a full sentence including terminal punctuation, not a sub-span) and line 120 '**Orchestrators sequence and gate, never reimplement.**' (6 words, full sentence). Chunk 7 '## What's special about this stack' (155-159): same pattern on all 5 bullets, e.g. line 158 '**Mandatory gates fire positionally.** `/ui` doesn't fire at session start...'; even bullets whose bold span is <=5 words (line 155 '**Front-loaded read-only analysis.**' = 3 words) still bold the WHOLE lead sentence, which is the rule's own named violation shape verbatim ('every bullet on a slide opens with a bolded sentence ... flatten to handles or prose'). Checked chunk 1's own new bolding (line 11: **explicit load**, **orchestrator sequencing**, **routing dispatch**, **hand-off pipelines**) against the same test: each is a short coined term (2-3 words) inline in prose, not a whole clause, and the four together name the page's four composition mechanisms introduced as a set -- reads as the rule's own 'consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' allowance generalised to one-handle-per-mechanism, not the monoculture shape. No maintainer accept-note covers the two flagged chunks.
